subject: Endocrine
subtopic: Pituitary gland anatomy and hormone subclasses
vignette: A first-year medical student is reviewing the embryologic origins of the two lobes of the pituitary gland during a anatomy lab. She notes that the anterior and posterior lobes arise from different germ layers.
question: The anterior pituitary (adenohypophysis) is derived from which of the following embryonic tissues?
explanation_correct: The adenohypophysis develops from an invagination of oral ectoderm known as Rathke pouch. This contrasts with the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis), which is derived from neuroectoderm. Remembering the separate origins helps explain why the two lobes have different cell types and regulatory inputs.

explanation_incorrect.A: Neuroectoderm gives rise to the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) and the hypothalamus, not the anterior lobe.
explanation_incorrect.C: Mesoderm gives rise to structures such as the adrenal cortex, not the anterior pituitary.
explanation_incorrect.D: Endoderm of the primitive pharynx forms thyroid follicular cells, not the pituitary gland.
explanation_incorrect.E: Neural crest contributes to the adrenal medulla and other structures, not the anterior pituitary.

educationalObjective: The anterior pituitary develops from oral ectoderm (Rathke pouch), whereas the posterior pituitary develops from neuroectoderm.

subject: Endocrine
subtopic: Pituitary gland anatomy and hormone subclasses
vignette: A researcher is cataloguing the hormones secreted by the different lobes of the pituitary gland. She notes that one hormone is produced by the intermediate lobe rather than by the adenohypophysis proper, and that this hormone contributes to pigmentation in certain disease states.
question: Which of the following hormones is secreted by the intermediate lobe of the pituitary?
explanation_correct: Melanotropin (MSH) is secreted by the intermediate lobe of the pituitary. The anterior pituitary, by contrast, secretes FSH, LH, ACTH, TSH, prolactin, GH, and beta-endorphin (FLAT PeG). MSH is also a POMC derivative, which is why states of excess ACTH can produce hyperpigmentation.

explanation_incorrect.A: FSH is an anterior pituitary gonadotropin produced by basophils, not a product of the intermediate lobe.
explanation_incorrect.B: Growth hormone is secreted by anterior pituitary acidophils, not by the intermediate lobe.
explanation_incorrect.C: Prolactin is secreted by anterior pituitary acidophils (lactotrophs), not by the intermediate lobe.
explanation_incorrect.E: ACTH is an anterior pituitary basophil product derived from POMC, not a hormone of the intermediate lobe.

educationalObjective: MSH is secreted by the intermediate lobe of the pituitary, while FLAT PeG hormones come from the anterior pituitary.

subject: Endocrine
subtopic: Pituitary gland anatomy and hormone subclasses
vignette: A biochemistry instructor is explaining why immunoassays for TSH, LH, FSH, and hCG must target a specific region to avoid cross-reactivity. These four glycoprotein hormones are structurally related and share one subunit.
question: Which subunit is common to TSH, LH, FSH, and hCG, such that hormone specificity is conferred by the other subunit?
explanation_correct: TSH, LH, FSH, and hCG share a common alpha subunit, while the beta subunit determines hormone specificity. This structural relationship is why clinical immunoassays are directed against the unique beta subunit to distinguish among these hormones, and it explains their overlapping biologic activity at high concentrations.

explanation_incorrect.B: The beta subunit is the hormone-specific subunit that confers specificity, not the subunit shared among the four hormones.
explanation_incorrect.C: There is no gamma subunit in this family of glycoprotein hormones.
explanation_incorrect.D: Carbohydrate content modulates hormone activity and clearance but is not the shared peptide subunit that defines this hormone family.
explanation_incorrect.E: POMC is the precursor of ACTH, MSH, and beta-endorphin, not a subunit of the glycoprotein hormones.

educationalObjective: TSH, LH, FSH, and hCG share a common alpha subunit; the beta subunit determines hormone specificity.

subject: Endocrine
subtopic: Pituitary gland anatomy and hormone subclasses
vignette: A patient with Cushing disease has markedly elevated ACTH. Her clinician notes that excessive ACTH is often accompanied by increased skin pigmentation because ACTH, MSH, and beta-endorphin are generated together from the same precursor molecule.
question: ACTH, MSH, and beta-endorphin are all derived from which of the following precursor molecules?
explanation_correct: Proopiomelanocortin (POMC) is cleaved to produce beta-endorphin, ACTH, and MSH, remembered by the mnemonic "Go pro with a BAM!" Because ACTH and MSH share this precursor, conditions with markedly elevated ACTH (such as Cushing disease or primary adrenal insufficiency) raise MSH and can cause hyperpigmentation.

explanation_incorrect.A: The common alpha subunit belongs to TSH, LH, FSH, and hCG and is not the precursor of ACTH, MSH, or beta-endorphin.
explanation_incorrect.B: Preproinsulin is the precursor of insulin and C-peptide in pancreatic beta cells, not of POMC derivatives.
explanation_incorrect.C: Prolactin is a distinct anterior pituitary hormone and is not a precursor for ACTH, MSH, or beta-endorphin.
explanation_incorrect.D: Preproglucagon is the precursor of glucagon and related peptides in the pancreas and intestine, not of POMC derivatives.

educationalObjective: POMC is the common precursor of beta-endorphin, ACTH, and MSH, linking ACTH excess to MSH-mediated hyperpigmentation.

subject: Endocrine
subtopic: Pituitary gland anatomy and hormone subclasses
vignette: A histology slide of the anterior pituitary shows clusters of basophilic cells adjacent to eosinophilic cells. A student is asked to identify which hormones are produced by the basophil population.
question: Which of the following combinations of hormones is produced by basophils of the anterior pituitary?
explanation_correct: Anterior pituitary basophils produce FSH, LH, ACTH, and TSH, captured by the mnemonic B-FLAT. Acidophils produce prolactin and GH (Acid PiG), while ADH and oxytocin are stored in the posterior pituitary. This staining-based classification is a classic way to organize anterior pituitary hormone products.

explanation_incorrect.A: Prolactin and GH are acidophil products (Acid PiG), not basophil products.
explanation_incorrect.B: GH is an acidophil product; only TSH in this pair is produced by basophils.
explanation_incorrect.D: MSH comes from the intermediate lobe, and prolactin and GH are acidophil products, not basophil products.
explanation_incorrect.E: ADH and oxytocin are synthesized in the hypothalamus and stored in the posterior neurohypophysis, not produced by anterior pituitary basophils.

educationalObjective: Anterior pituitary basophils secrete FSH, LH, ACTH, and TSH (B-FLAT); acidophils secrete prolactin and GH (Acid PiG).

subject: Endocrine
subtopic: Pituitary gland anatomy and hormone subclasses
vignette: A patient sustains a head injury and develops diabetes insipidus. Imaging localizes a small lesion to the posterior pituitary. A student reviews the normal physiology of this region before answering a question about it.
question: Which of the following statements about the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) is correct?

options.text: It synthesizes ADH and oxytocin within its own resident cells.
It stores and releases ADH and oxytocin made in hypothalamic supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei.
It is derived from oral ectoderm of Rathke pouch.
It secretes the gonadotropins FSH and LH.
It is composed predominantly of chromaffin cells.

explanation_correct: The neurohypophysis stores and releases ADH and oxytocin that are synthesized in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus and transported to the posterior pituitary along axons via neurophysin carrier proteins. It is derived from neuroectoderm. It does not synthesize the hormones itself—it is a storage and release site.

explanation_incorrect.A: The posterior pituitary does not synthesize these hormones; they are made in the hypothalamus and only stored and released by the posterior lobe.
explanation_incorrect.C: Oral ectoderm (Rathke pouch) forms the anterior pituitary, not the posterior lobe, which is neuroectodermal.
explanation_incorrect.D: FSH and LH are anterior pituitary gonadotropins secreted by basophils, not by the posterior pituitary.
explanation_incorrect.E: Chromaffin cells are found in the adrenal medulla, not in the posterior pituitary.

educationalObjective: The posterior pituitary stores and releases hypothalamically derived ADH and oxytocin transported via neurophysins and is derived from neuroectoderm.
